moments.label: Identifying POI levels
moments.why: Instructor introduces the three key price levels: previous daily high, low, and close as the core POIs for trading.

moments.label: Focusing on daily candles
moments.why: Instructor specifies that the system will focus only on daily candles for identifying setups.

moments.label: Marking three levels on chart
moments.why: Instructor explains marking out the previous daily high, low, and close on the chart as foundational elements.

moments.label: Two setups: sweep and break retest
moments.why: Instructor introduces the two primary trading setups based on previous daily candle: swing failure (sweep) and break and retest.

moments.label: Break and retest pattern example
moments.why: Instructor points to a specific chart example showing break and retest off the previous daily high.

moments.label: Continuation and reversal setups
moments.why: Instructor explains that both continuation (break and retest) and reversal (swing failure) patterns are valid setups.

moments.label: Anchor bar concept
moments.why: Instructor defines the previous daily candle as the 'anchor bar' for all trading decisions.

moments.label: Inside bars as noise
moments.why: Instructor identifies inside candles as consolidation and advises treating them as market noise.

moments.label: Illustrating swing failure pattern
moments.why: Instructor shows a schematic of the swing failure pattern, highlighting price sweeping and reversing.

moments.label: Break and retest example
moments.why: Instructor points to a chart showing break and retest of previous daily low with price moving higher.

moments.label: Trading the candle as it happens
moments.why: Instructor emphasizes entering trades immediately after price breaks and retests, without waiting for candle close.

moments.label: Introducing environment concept
moments.why: Instructor introduces the idea of market environment using a three-day cycle to determine context.

moments.label: Three-day cycle explanation
moments.why: Instructor explains the market's tendency to push three times (three green or red days) before reversal.

moments.label: Monday as expansion day
moments.why: Instructor describes Monday as typically a trend-expanding day, contrary to common belief.

moments.label: Tuesday as continuation day
moments.why: Instructor explains Tuesday is usually a trend continuation day.

moments.label: Three green days leading to short bias
moments.why: Instructor explains that after three consecutive green days, the market is likely exhausted and bias shifts to short.
